items.label: Theorem 1
items.title: General strong-Wolfe counterexample
items.statement:
\label{thm:main}
There exist $f\in C^2(\R^n)$, $x_0$, $H_0\succ0$ and positive step
lengths generating an infinite classical DFP sequence satisfying
\eqref{eq:armijo} and \eqref{eq:strong-curvature}, with
\[
 (1-\varepsilon)I\preceq\nabla^2f(x)\preceq(1+\varepsilon)I
 \quad(x\in\R^n),\qquad \|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to1.
\]
The Hessian is globally $\beta$-H\"older continuous and admits no
$\beta'$-H\"older bound on $\mathcal L_0$ for any $\beta'\in(\beta,1]$.
The origin is the unique minimizer, and the accumulation set is the
unit circle in a two-dimensional subspace of $\R^n$.

The origin is the unique minimizer, and the accumulation set is the unit circle in a two-dimensional subspace of $\R^n$.

items.statementHtml: Under these assumptions, every classical DFP sequence with positive step lengths satisfying [eq:armijo]--[eq:weak-curvature] either reaches the unique minimizer $x_*$ in finitely many iterations or satisfies $x_k\to x_*$ and $\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0$.

/-- Lemma 3 of `20251124-DFP/MP.zip`: the exact polar step interface.
The source search step, positive step length, inverse DFP update, and raw
matrix recurrence are exposed on one actual `Parameters` orbit. -/

items.label: Lemma 3
items.title: Exact polar search step, curvature, and DFP update
items.statementHtml: Fix $k\ge0$. Suppose that $\rho_k,\rho_{k+1},\zeta_k,\zeta_{k+1}>0$, $Z_k\succ0$, $(Z_k)_{12}>0$, and $0<\delta_k<\pi$. Then the following statements hold. \item[\textup{i)}] There exists a positive step length $\alpha_k$ satisfying $s_k=-\alpha_kH_kg_k$ if and only if r_k=\cos\delta_k+h_k\sin\delta_k. In this case, the step length $\alpha_k$ is unique and is given by [eq:fixed-realization]. \item[\textup{ii)}] If [eq:fixed-step] and $p_k^Tq_k>0$ hold, then $s_k^Ty_k>0$ and the DFP update [eq:dfp-update] is equivalent to Z_{k+1}=R(\delta_k)^T \left[\left(I-\frac{q_kp_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k}\right)Z_k \left(I-\frac{p_kq_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k}\right) +\frac{q_kq_k^T}{p_k^Tq_k}\right]R(\delta_k)\succ0.

theorem lemma3_matrixStep (p : Parameters) (hβ : 0 < p.beta)
    (hstart : 0 < p.startIndex) (k : ℕ)
    (hZ : (p.matrix k).PosDef) (hC : 0 < p.matrix k 0 1)
    (hsin : 0 < Real.sin (p.angleIncrement k))
    (hr : 0 < p.radiusRatio k)
    (hbalance : p.radius k = p.radiusRatio k * p.radius (k + 1))
    (hrNext : 0 < p.radius (k + 1))
    (hσ : 0 < DFP.Polar.sigmaOf (p.matrix k) (p.angleIncrement k)
      (p.zeta k) (p.zeta (k + 1))) :
    p.matrix (k + 1) = DFP.Polar.matrixStep (p.matrix k) (p.angleIncrement k)
        (p.zeta k) (p.zeta (k + 1)) ∧
      0 < p.stepLength k ∧
      WithLp.ofLp (p.point (k + 1) - p.point k) =
        (-p.stepLength k) •
          (p.inverseHessian k *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp (p.gradients k)) ∧
      0 < WithLp.ofLp (p.point (k + 1) - p.point k) ⬝ᵥ
        WithLp.ofLp (p.gradients (k + 1) - p.gradients k) ∧
      p.inverseHessian (k + 1) = Matrix.inverseDFPUpdate (p.inverseHessian k)
        (WithLp.ofLp (p.point (k + 1) - p.point k))
        (WithLp.ofLp (p.gradients (k + 1) - p.gradients k)) := by
  refine ⟨Parameters.matrix_step p hβ hstart k, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact p.stepLength_pos k hZ hC hsin hr
  · exact p.chord_search k hZ hC hr hbalance
  · exact p.secant_pairing_pos k hbalance hrNext hsin hσ
  · exact p.inverseHessian_step hβ hstart k hbalance hZ
      hrNext hsin hσ

items.label: Theorem 4
items.title: Source witness for the fixed Wolfe pair and exponent
items.statement:
\label{thm:concrete}
There exists $\bar\sigma>0$ such that, for each fixed
$0<\sigma_*<\bar\sigma$ and all sufficiently large $j_0$, the construction
is well defined and yields a uniformly convex $f\in C^2(\R^2)$ with
a globally $1/2$-H\"older Hessian satisfying
\eqref{eq:prescribed-jets}--\eqref{eq:fixed-hessian-bound}.
The positive step lengths \eqref{eq:fixed-realization} generate exactly
$\{x_k,H_k\}$ by classical DFP with strong Wolfe parameters $(1/4,1/2)$,
with $\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to1$ and the unit circle as accumulation set.

items.label: Lemma 5
items.title: Analytic one-step polar limit
items.statementHtml: Fix $X\succ0$ with $X_{12}>0$ and put $Z=S_\tau^{-1}XS_\tau^{-1}$. Suppose $\delta=\bar\delta\tau$ with $\bar\delta>0$ fixed and $\zeta,\zeta_+\to1$ as $\tau\downarrow0$. Then $p^Tq>0$ for all sufficiently small $\tau>0$, and the update [eq:fixed-scaled-update] satisfies S_\tau Z_+S_\tau\longrightarrow L_{\bar\delta}(X) = \gamma&\gamma(\bar h-\bar\delta)\\ \gamma(\bar h-\bar\delta)&1+\gamma(\bar h-\bar\delta)^2 . The limit is positive definite and has determinant $\gamma$.

items.label: Lemma 6
items.title: Local two-step continuation bounds
items.statementHtml: The map $\Phi(\tau^2,t,\gamma,u)$ defined in [eq:fixed-two-step-map] extends analytically to a neighborhood of $(0,0,\gamma_*,0)$. For sufficiently small $\tau^2,t\ge0$ in this neighborhood, it satisfies &\|u_+\|_*\le \kappa_1\|u\|_*+\kappa_2(t+\tau^2), \\ &\gamma_+=\gamma-\frac43 t(\gamma-\gamma_*) +O(t\|u\|_*+t^2+\tau^2), for a fixed norm $\|\cdot\|_*$, $0<\kappa_1<1$, and $\kappa_2>0$. The estimates are uniform on sufficiently small closed neighborhoods of $\gamma_*$ and $u=0$. For $\tau>0$ in these neighborhoods, both stages are well defined with $Z\succ0$, $Z_{12}>0$, and $r,p^Tq>0$.

theorem lemma7_fixedContinuation (p : Parameters) (hβ : 0 < p.beta) (hβone : p.beta < 1) :
    ∃ N > 0, ∃ M > 0, ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∃ J : ℕ, 0 < J ∧ ∀ j0 : ℕ, J ≤ j0 →
      Continuation.TrajectoryBounds p j0 N M ∧
        (∀ j : ℕ,
          Continuation.fastSize p (Continuation.stateAt p j0 j) ≤
              N / ((j0 + j : ℕ) : ℝ) ∧
            |Continuation.slowError p (Continuation.stateAt p j0 j)| ≤
              M * scale p.beta j0 j ^ (1 - p.beta)) ∧
        (∀ k : ℕ, Continuation.RawFeasible (p.withStartIndex j0) k) ∧
        ∀ j : ℕ,

              p.oddReference (Continuation.stateAt p j0 j).1‖ ≤

  obtain ⟨N, hN, M, hM, K, hK, J, hJ, h⟩ :=
    Continuation.existsContinuationEstimates p hβ hβone
  refine ⟨N, hN, M, hM, K, hK, J, hJ, ?_⟩
  intro j0 hj0
  obtain ⟨htrajectory, hraw, hodd⟩ := h j0 hj0
  refine ⟨htrajectory, ?_, hraw, hodd⟩
  intro j
  exact ⟨htrajectory.fast_bound j, htrajectory.slow_bound j⟩

/-- Lemma 8 of `20251124-DFP/MP.zip`: the actual points have uniform
separation, linear step bounds and the complete unit-circle cluster set. -/

items.label: Lemma 8
items.title: Fixed geometry and Wolfe verification
items.statement:
\label{lem:fixed-geometry}
For sufficiently large $j_0$, the tail products in
\eqref{eq:fixed-radii} converge and satisfy $\rho_k\downarrow1$.
The accumulation set of the prescribed points is the unit circle
$\Gamma$, and there is a constant $\kappa>0$, independent of $j_0$,
such that for every $m\ne k$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-separation}
 \|x_m-x_k\|\ge\kappa
 \max\{\tau_{\lfloor m/2\rfloor},\tau_{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}\}.
\end{equation}
The prescribed values $\rho_k^2/2$ and gradients $g_k$ satisfy the
strong Wolfe conditions with $(\eta_1,\eta_2)=(1/4,1/2)$.

/-- Corollary 12 of `20251124-DFP/MP.zip`: identity initialization in every
finite dimension at least two. -/

items.label: Corollary 12
items.title: Identity initialization
items.statement:
\label{cor:identity-initialization}
For every $n\ge2$, $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, and $\beta\in(0,1)$,
there exist $\widetilde f\in C^2(\R^n)$ and $\widetilde x_0$ such that
$\nabla^2\widetilde f$ is globally $\beta$-H\"older continuous and
$mI\preceq\nabla^2\widetilde f(x)\preceq MI$ on $\R^n$, for some
$0<m\le M<\infty$. Classical DFP from $(\widetilde x_0,I)$ admits an
infinite strong Wolfe sequence with parameters $\eta_1,\eta_2$ and
$\liminf_k\|\nabla\widetilde f(\widetilde x_k)\|>0$.
Its accumulation set is an ellipse centered at the origin in a
two-dimensional subspace.
items.statementHtml: For every $n\ge2$, $0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1$, and $ eta\in(0,1)$, there exist $\widetilde f\in C^2(\R^n)$ and $\widetilde x_0$ such that $ abla^2\widetilde f$ is globally $ eta$-H\"older continuous and $mI\preceq abla^2\widetilde f(x)\preceq MI$ on $\R^n$, for some $0<m\le M<\infty$. Classical DFP from $(\widetilde x_0,I)$ admits an infinite strong Wolfe sequence with parameters $\eta_1,\eta_2$ and $\liminf_k\| abla\widetilde f(\widetilde x_k)\|>0$. Its accumulation set is an ellipse centered at the origin in a two-dimensional subspace.
